topic: Bridging Dimensions: Space-Filling Curves and the Infinite
target_audience: University students (STEM majors or math enthusiasts)

sections.title: The Dimensional Intuition (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: A plane exists in two dimensions.
Can a one-dimensional line fill space?
animations: Show line spanning partially across the square in #FF0000.
Display label '1D Line vs 2D Area' in #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Peano Construction: A Recursive Logic (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: Giuseppe Peano discovered a space-filling path.
Iteratively divide the square into smaller parts.
Connect the path through each iteration.
The path densifies with each step.
This recursion approaches the infinite limit.
animations: Divide the square grid iteratively in #FF00FF.
Animate path connection through iterations in #FFFF00.
Show path densifying across the square in #00FFFF.

sections.title: Finite Rules, Infinite Results (2:00-3:30)
lecture_lines: The limit reaches every point inside.
The mapping is continuous, not injective.
Infinite complexity arises from simple rules.
animations: Expand the segment to fill the interior in #00FF00.
Animate ant crossing all grid squares in #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Bridge: Bridging Discrete and Continuous (3:30-4:30)
lecture_lines: Algorithms bridge discrete steps and continuous space.
This provides the basis for fractals.
Hilbert curves optimize data cache storage.
animations: Animate computer icon connecting discrete to continuous in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Summary & Reflection (4:30-5:00)
lecture_lines: Dimensions are limits to be traversed.
Math and art converge elegantly here.
